ai.title: Hosting backend mode flips from convex to shadow
ai.summary: The `HOSTING_BACKEND` constant in `common/src/constants/hosting-backend.ts` changes from 'convex' to 'shadow' to activate the shadow-read mode of the hosting Postgres migration. In this mode, Convex continues to serve all hosting reads and writes, while server paths additionally read the Postgres copy maintained by the `hosting.projection` chain. The change enables logging of `convex_pg_shadow_row_mismatch` with column names only to verify consistency between the stores before fully switching to Postgres.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/hosting-backend.ts`, the export constant `HOSTING_BACKEND` value changed from 'convex' to 'shadow'.

You notice no changes in your daily use of the assistant, as your hosting remains fully served by the stable original system.

ai.title: Add CLI product funnel telemetry and run conversion tracking
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now emits `PRODUCT_FUNNEL_STEP` analytics events for user journey stages from launch through turn completion, gated behind the `IS_FREEBUFF` constant. A new `createCliRunFunnel` state machine in the CLI tracks dispatch, start, and response events to classify a run as succeeded, failed, or cancelled based on whether useful root output was produced. The `createRunConfig` utility exposes optional `observeEvent` and `observeChunk` hooks that pipe SDK stream events to this funnel logic without interfering with the agent loop, while a strict Zod schema in the common package rejects payloads containing prompts, paths, or auth identifiers.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `common/src/constants/product-funnel.ts` defining `PRODUCT_FUNNEL_EVENT` and a Zod schema, introduces `cli/src/utils/cli-product-funnel.ts` and `cli/src/utils/cli-run-funnel.ts`, and modifies `cli/src/utils/create-run-config.ts` to accept optional `observeEvent` and `observeChunk` callbacks that forward SDK events to the funnel state machine.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the specific PostHog dashboard or Axiom query that consumes these funnel events for conversion rate analysis.

changes.what: Defines the closed Zod schema and event constant for product funnel telemetry, rejecting any payload containing sensitive data like prompts or file paths.
Implements the native CLI funnel capture logic and run-level state machine that tracks conversion outcomes from user input to model response.
Integrates funnel capture calls into the login, project picker, model selection, and chat input components to record stage transitions.
Marks the new funnel event as always-tracked in the analytics sampler to ensure consistent denominator for conversion rate calculations.

facts: Chat text is data, but Render's WAF can mistake it for executable commands. The mirror server unwraps this UTF-8 JSON envelope after authentication. This is transport encoding, not encryption. Deploy the decoder first.
entries.title: New shared/core files landed

ai.title: Add base64 mirror request encoding for WAF bypass
ai.summary: A new utility in `common` adds `encodeMirrorRequest` to encode outgoing payloads into a base64 JSON envelope. The module docblock states that Render's Web Application Firewall (WAF) can misinterpret raw chat text as executable commands, so this transport encoding (not encryption) allows the mirror server to safely unwrap the data after authentication.
ai.evidence: The diff adds the new file `common/src/util/mirror-request.ts` exporting `encodeMirrorRequest`, which wraps a payload in a base64 JSON envelope with the comment noting Render's WAF can mistake chat text for executable commands.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which HTTP client or server call invokes this new encoder.

eli5.text: The team added a new internal tool to prepare data in a specific, safe format before it is sent to a secondary server. This process helps prevent a security filter from accidentally blocking normal conversation data while the system is being tested. This change only affects the people who manage the Freebuff service and does not alter how you use the assistant.
